newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 19.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The leadership of ruling party PASOK is troubled by growing dissatisfaction within the party blocking consensus on major issues such as Greek-Turkish relations and proposed changes to the job market. Sources say senior cadres will try to smooth over problems by autumn next year in the run-up to preparations for the next general elections.
--Greek pop idol Sakis Rouvas and his Turkish counterpart Burak Cut will give a concert in the UN buffer zone in Cyprus today amidst growing criticism and possible demonstrations.

--Some 46.0 percent of Greeks interviewed in a recent poll gave a vote of confidence to Prime Minister Costas Simitis, saying he was the most appropriate premier. Conservative opposition New Democracy leader Costas Karamanlis culled 31.7 percent. Ruling party PASOK also received more support than ND on being the best able to deal with major issues.
--The fall in interest rates is soon to be followed by taxes of 7.5 to 12 percent on the interest from bonds and treasury bills, according to reports.

--The government is planning a package of measures to cut back on spending on pharmaceuticals dispensed by pension funds and hospitals. The final decisions are to be taken today at the economic policy committee meeting.
